description:
We are APEX EXODUS, a team of two passionate innovators participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in space technology Earth observation, remote sensing, geospatial intelligence, climate science and AI-driven innovation.

We transform complex satellite data into meaningful insights and develop innovative solutions to real-world environmental challenges. We welcome curious creative and collaborative minds who are passionate about science and exploring beyond boundaries.

FLAGWA

Reading Earth's Changing Surface Through Radar

FLAGWA is an interactive radar remote-sensing platform designed to help people explore and understand changes across Earth's surface using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, with a particular focus on NASA–ISRO NISAR mission observations.

Our flagship study area is Kuttanad, Alappuzha, Kerala, India — a unique wetland landscape where agriculture, waterways, soil conditions and managed water levels are closely interconnected. These changing conditions make Kuttanad an important place to explore how radar observations can reveal patterns that may not be visible through ordinary optical imagery.

FLAGWA brings radar data exploration, comparative analysis and geospatial visualisation into one platform. Its key experiences include the Explorer, Radar Lab, Earthscore and Groundwire, helping users move from satellite observations towards interpretable, location-specific insights.

The project explores how changes in radar backscatter can help identify areas that deserve further investigation. It also emphasises scientific responsibility: a radar signal change alone does not confirm flooding or establish its cause. Results need to be interpreted alongside environmental context and independent ground-based or complementary data.

Our vision is to make complex radar observations more accessible to students, researchers and environmental practitioners.
details:
FLAGWA — Global Surface Change Explorer

Reading Earth's Changing Surface Through Radar

1. What is FLAGWA?

FLAGWA is an interactive geospatial platform that explores Earth's changing surface using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite observations, with a particular focus on NASA–ISRO's NISAR mission.

Our goal is to make complex radar remote-sensing data more accessible, understandable and useful for students, researchers and environmental practitioners.

We selected Kuttanad, Alappuzha, Kerala, India, as our flagship study area. Known as the Rice Bowl of Kerala, Kuttanad is a unique wetland ecosystem where agriculture, waterways, soil conditions and managed water levels constantly interact. Understanding these changes is important for environmental monitoring and sustainable landscape management.

2. How does it work?

FLAGWA brings satellite data exploration, geospatial processing, visualisation and environmental context into a unified platform.

The workflow consists of:

  • Data Discovery: Accessing and exploring relevant SAR observations and satellite datasets, including NISAR products.
  • Radar Exploration: Visualising radar observations and comparing acquisitions to investigate changes over time.
  • Radar Lab: Providing analytical workflows to process and investigate radar observations.
  • Earthscore: Presenting interpreted environmental and surface-change information in an accessible format.
  • Groundwire: Connecting satellite observations with geographical and environmental context to support further investigation.

Users can explore locations, examine radar observations, compare datasets and investigate potential surface changes through an interactive interface.

3. Our scientific approach

SAR technology is particularly valuable because it uses microwave signals and can collect observations regardless of daylight and through many cloud conditions.

FLAGWA explores how changes in radar backscatter may reflect differences in surface conditions, including open water, flooded vegetation, wet soil and agricultural activity.

Our Kuttanad case study investigates changes between two L-band NISAR GCOV observations from 29 October 2026 and 10 November 2026.

An important part of our approach is scientific responsibility. A change in radar backscatter does not automatically confirm flooding, identify flood depth or establish its cause. Results must be interpreted with additional information such as rainfall, water levels, agricultural cycles, hydrological conditions and independent observations.

FLAGWA is designed to support this investigation rather than present every detected change as a confirmed environmental event.

4. Benefits and intended impact

  • Environmental understanding: Helps users investigate changes in wetlands, agricultural landscapes and other surface environments.
  • Research accessibility: Makes radar data exploration more approachable for students and researchers.
  • Disaster and water research: Provides a platform for investigating potential water-related surface changes.
  • Education: Encourages practical learning in SAR remote sensing, GIS and Earth observation.
  • Evidence-based investigation: Promotes combining satellite observations with environmental context and independent validation.

Our long-term vision is to support environmental research, educational institutions and organisations working towards better understanding of Earth's changing landscapes.

5. Technology and tools used

Frontend

  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • React Router
  • TanStack Query
  • Zustand
  • MapLibre GL
  • GeoTIFF.js
  • Recharts

Backend and data processing

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • PostgreSQL with PostGIS
  • Redis and Celery
  • NASA Earthdata and ASF data access workflows
  • Raster and geospatial processing workflows

Visualisation and infrastructure

  • Interactive geospatial maps
  • Satellite raster visualisation
  • Cloud-compatible object storage architecture
  • REST APIs
  • Git and GitHub for version control and collaboration

6. What makes FLAGWA creative?

FLAGWA is not intended to be just another satellite imagery viewer. Its central idea is to create a journey from radar observations to environmental understanding.

Instead of showing users complicated satellite data without context, FLAGWA organises the experience around exploration, analysis and interpretation.

Its modular experiences Explorer, Radar Lab, Earthscore and Groundwire help connect technical radar observations with real-world environmental questions.

Our Kuttanad-first approach also gives the project a meaningful geographical identity: starting with a real wetland landscape and developing a workflow that can eventually be adapted to other regions.

7. Team and future vision

FLAGWA is developed by Anson Joseph (Team Lead) and Sharun Tomy, from Mar Thoma College, Thiruvalla, affiliated with Mahatma Gandhi University, Kerala.

We envision FLAGWA growing into an accessible Earth observation and environmental research platform that connects universities, remote-sensing researchers, environmental practitioners and communities.

Our mission is simple: make the invisible changes in Earth's surface easier to explore, investigate and understand.
